titulo: What Is the healthiest way to prepare vegetables?

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: The first kind wants to know how different cooking methods affect the nutrition in vegetables. The other kind of person wants to know how to eat more vegetables. Thomas’ simple answer to both groups is this: The best vegetables are the ones you actually want to eat.

Thomas told the Associated Press that many people buy vegetables that they think they will eat. Maybe the produce is popular or someone is bringing attention to it on social media. But then they end up not using it. That means the vegetable gets thrown away after it goes bad.

However, Thomas said research shows cooking methods do affect nutrition. But it is not as simple as comparing raw, or uncooked, vegetables to cooked ones. Cooking methods can include steaming, roasting, boiling, or sauteing.
When vegetables are cooked with high heat for a long period of time many nutrients break down. However, cooking softens the cell walls in vegetables, making them easier for the body to digest.
Cooking changes the structure of vegetables which increases what dietitians call bioavailability. This is the body’s ability to use the nutrients in vegetables, Thomas said.

Cooked food is often more nutritious than raw food. For example, cooked tomatoes release more of the antioxidant lycopene than raw tomatoes, she said. Lycopene is believed to have qualities that prevent cancer.

Also, cooked carrots have more beta-carotene that can be absorbed by the body. Roasting pumpkins, carrots and sweet potatoes increases available carotenoids. These antioxidants are thought to prevent inflammation in the body.
However, the shorter the cooking time, the more nutrients are kept in the food. That advice comes from Amber Pankonin, a dietitian in the U.S. state of Nebraska.
Cooking over boiling water, or steaming, and in a microwave are considered the most nutritious methods. These two methods use little time and require no fat.

Another healthy method is blanching. This is when you boil vegetables in water for a minute or two. But not too long. Boiling vegetables runs the risk of losing water-soluble nutrients including vitamin C, B1 and folate.
Dietitians say there is no problem using a small amount of fat. Besides making vegetables taste better, a little cooking oil helps the body to absorb fat-soluble vitamins, said Pankonin.

That means more vitamin A from squash, carrots, and sweet potatoes; more vitamin D from mushrooms; more vitamin E from bell peppers, leafy greens and asparagus; and more vitamin K from greens, broccoli and onions.
For pan frying or sauteing, Pankonin suggests cooking with enough oil so the vegetables do not stick to the pan. The amount of oil will depend on the quantity of vegetables and the size of the pan.
For roasting, you will likely need more oil. Despite the longer cooking time, roasting will still keep some nutrients and will increase the flavor with the heating of natural sugars.
titulo_es: What is the healthiest way to prepare vegetables?
resumen_es: Two dietitians explain how cooking methods affect the nutrients in vegetables: cooking can help the body make better use of them, but it should be brief and with a little oil.
nivel_motivo: The lexical index places it at C1 because of the nutrition terms (bioavailability, carotenoids, folate), but the sentences are short and the ideas simple and well explained, which corresponds to B2.

ideas_clave.idea: According to dietitian Thomas, the best vegetables are those people really want to eat, since many bought because they are trendy end up spoiling and being thrown away.
Cooking does influence nutrition in a complex way: long cooking at high heat destroys nutrients, but it also softens cell walls and makes vegetables easier to digest.
By changing their structure, cooking raises bioavailability, so cooked tomatoes, carrots or pumpkins can provide more antioxidants such as lycopene and carotenoids than raw ones.
Dietitian Amber Pankonin stresses that shorter cooking preserves more nutrients, which is why steaming and microwaving, quick and fat-free, are the healthiest methods.
Blanching for a minute or two is also healthy, whereas prolonged boiling makes vegetables lose water-soluble nutrients like vitamin C.
A little fat is not harmful: besides improving taste, oil helps the body absorb fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K from many vegetables.
For sautéing, just enough oil to prevent sticking is advised, while roasting needs more oil and longer cooking but still keeps some nutrients and enhances flavour.

resumen_modelo: The text examines how cooking methods affect the nutritional value of vegetables. According to the dietitian Thomas, the best vegetables are simply those people will actually eat, as fashionable produce often ends up being wasted. Research nevertheless shows that preparation matters. Although prolonged cooking at high temperatures destroys nutrients, cooking also softens cell walls and increases bioavailability, so that cooked tomatoes or carrots, for instance, provide more antioxidants than raw ones. Another dietitian, Amber Pankonin, recommends short cooking times, which makes steaming, microwaving and brief blanching the healthiest options, whereas long boiling removes water-soluble vitamins. Finally, a moderate amount of oil is beneficial, since it improves flavour and helps the body absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

preguntas.pregunta: According to Thomas, which vegetables are the best?
opciones: The ones you actually want to eat
The ones that are eaten raw
The ones that are popular on social media
The ones with the most vitamins
respuestas: The ones you actually want to eat
preguntas.cita: The best vegetables are the ones you actually want to eat.
preguntas.explicacion: Thomas replies that the best vegetables are the ones you actually want to eat. The ones that are popular on social media are precisely those that often end up being thrown away.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: People sometimes buy vegetables because they are trendy and then throw them away.
preguntas.cita: Maybe the produce is popular or someone is bringing attention to it on social media. But then they end up not using it.
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph 1 explains that people buy fashionable vegetables that are then not used and end up in the bin when they go off.

preguntas.enunciado: Find a word in paragraph 2 that means “not cooked”.
preguntas.cita: comparing raw, or uncooked, vegetables to cooked ones
preguntas.explicacion: “Raw” means not cooked (es: crudo); the text itself clarifies it with the synonym “uncooked”.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Cooking vegetables makes them harder for the body to digest.
preguntas.cita: cooking softens the cell walls in vegetables, making them easier for the body to digest
preguntas.explicacion: It is the other way round: cooking softens the cell walls and makes vegetables easier to digest.

preguntas.enunciado: Find a term in paragraph 4 that means “the body’s ability to make use of nutrients”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a term meaning 'the body's ability to use nutrients'.
preguntas.explicacion: “Bioavailability” (es: biodisponibilidad) is, according to the text, the body’s ability to use nutrients.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the benefit of cooking tomatoes, according to the text?
preguntas.cita: cooked tomatoes release more of the antioxidant lycopene than raw tomatoes
preguntas.explicacion: Cooked tomatoes release more lycopene. Vitamin C is mentioned in connection with boiling, in which it is actually lost, and oil is not linked to tomatoes.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Roasting carrots and sweet potatoes increases the carotenoids available to the body.
preguntas.cita: Roasting pumpkins, carrots and sweet potatoes increases available carotenoids.
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph 6 states it word for word: roasting squash, carrots and sweet potatoes increases the available carotenoids.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are steaming and microwaving considered the most nutritious methods?
opciones: They are quick and require no fat.
They remove the cell walls completely.
They add natural sugars to vegetables.
respuestas: They are quick and require no fat.
preguntas.cita: These two methods use little time and require no fat.
preguntas.explicacion: They are the most nutritious because they require little time and no fat. Prolonged high temperatures destroy nutrients, and natural sugars are mentioned in connection with roasting.

preguntas.enunciado: Answer in your own words (1–3 sentences).
preguntas.pregunta: What is blanching, and why should vegetables not be boiled for too long?
respuestas: Blanching means boiling vegetables in water for only a minute or two. Longer boiling can make them lose water-soluble nutrients such as vitamin C, vitamin B1 and folate.
preguntas.cita: This is when you boil vegetables in water for a minute or two.
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph 9 defines blanching and warns that boiling for a long time causes the loss of water-soluble nutrients.

preguntas.enunciado: Find an adjective in paragraph 9 that means “that dissolves in water”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an adjective meaning 'able to dissolve in water'.
preguntas.cita: runs the risk of losing water-soluble nutrients including vitamin C, B1 and folate
preguntas.explicacion: “Water-soluble” means that it dissolves in water (es: hidrosoluble); it is the opposite of “fat-soluble” (es: liposoluble), which appears in paragraph 10.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Dietitians advise cooking vegetables without any fat at all.
preguntas.cita: Dietitians say there is no problem using a small amount of fat.
preguntas.explicacion: The dietitians say that a small amount of fat is not a problem and even helps to absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

preguntas.pregunta: Which vitamin does the text associate with mushrooms?
preguntas.explicacion: The text links mushrooms with vitamin D. Vitamin A is associated with squash, carrots and sweet potatoes; E, with peppers and asparagus; K, with broccoli and onions.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Pankonin recommends olive oil as the best oil for sauteing vegetables.
preguntas.explicacion: The text talks about the amount of oil for sautéing, but does not mention any particular type of oil.

preguntas.enunciado: Answer in your own words (1–3 sentences).
preguntas.pregunta: Is roasting a good option despite the long cooking time? Explain.
respuestas: Yes, to some extent: roasting requires more oil and a longer time, but it still preserves some nutrients and makes vegetables tastier because their natural sugars are heated.
preguntas.cita: Despite the longer cooking time, roasting will still keep some nutrients and will increase the flavor with the heating of natural sugars.
preguntas.explicacion: The last paragraph adds a nuance: roasting is not the most nutritious method, but it keeps some of the nutrients and improves the flavour.
